findings.explanation: 'quickly' is vague; a tester cannot set a pass/fail limit from it.
findings.question_for_author: What measurable criterion does 'quickly' stand for?
findings.requirement_text: The cluster should wake up quickly when a door is opened.

findings.explanation: 'adequate' is vague; a tester cannot set a pass/fail limit from it.
findings.question_for_author: What measurable criterion does 'adequate' stand for?
findings.requirement_text: The chime volume should be adequate for all driving conditions.

findings.explanation: 'appropriately' is vague; a tester cannot set a pass/fail limit from it.
findings.question_for_author: What measurable criterion does 'appropriately' stand for?
findings.requirement_text: The cluster shall protect cryptographic keys appropriately.

findings.explanation: 'smoothly' is vague; a tester cannot set a pass/fail limit from it.
findings.question_for_author: What measurable criterion does 'smoothly' stand for?
findings.requirement_text: The graphics shall run smoothly at all times.

findings.explanation: The content of the goodbye screen is not defined anywhere in the set, so a tester cannot verify that the correct screen is shown.
findings.question_for_author: Where is the goodbye screen defined and what must it contain?
findings.requirement_text: When IGN changes from ON to OFF, the cluster shall display the goodbye screen for 3 s.

findings.explanation: No maximum time is given between the end of the goodbye screen and entry into SLEEP, so the transition timing cannot be checked.
findings.question_for_author: What is the maximum time between the end of the goodbye screen and the cluster entering the SLEEP state?
findings.requirement_text: After displaying the goodbye screen, the cluster shall enter the SLEEP state.

findings.explanation: It is not stated which state the cluster must reach on waking or from which state this applies, so the expected end state cannot be verified.
findings.question_for_author: From which state does this apply, and which state must the cluster enter when it wakes up?
findings.requirement_text: The cluster should wake up quickly when a door is opened.

findings.explanation: It is unclear whether 'actual vehicle speed' means the true ground speed or the VehicleSpeed signal value that G06 requires to be displayed, which changes both the test reference and whether an offset must be applied.
findings.question_for_author: Is 'actual vehicle speed' the VehicleSpeed signal value or an independently measured true speed, and how does this relate to displaying the received value as required in G06?
findings.requirement_text: The displayed speed shall never be lower than the actual vehicle speed.

findings.explanation: The fuel level range each segment represents is not given, so the correct number of lit segments for a given fuel level cannot be checked.
findings.question_for_author: Which fuel level thresholds correspond to each of the eight segments being lit?
findings.requirement_text: The cluster shall display the fuel level as a bar graph with eight segments.

findings.explanation: No permitted variation or filter characteristic is specified, so there is no pass/fail limit for fluctuation.
findings.question_for_author: What maximum change in the displayed fuel level, over what time, is permitted while the actual fuel quantity is constant?
findings.requirement_text: The fuel level display shall be filtered so that it does not fluctuate when the vehicle is driving on an incline.

findings.explanation: The incline gradient and duration the filter must handle are not specified, so the test conditions cannot be defined.
findings.question_for_author: What range of incline gradients and durations must the filter compensate for?
findings.requirement_text: The fuel level display shall be filtered so that it does not fluctuate when the vehicle is driving on an incline.

findings.evidence: the fuel level is below 10 percent
findings.explanation: It is unclear whether the threshold applies to the raw or the filtered fuel level from G13, and when the telltale is switched off again is not stated.
findings.question_for_author: Is the 10 percent threshold evaluated on the raw or the filtered fuel level, and under which condition is the low-fuel telltale switched off?
findings.requirement_text: When the fuel level is below 10 percent, the low-fuel telltale shall be lit.

findings.explanation: No maximum delay between BrakeWarn becoming 1 and the telltale lighting is given, so the response cannot be checked.
findings.question_for_author: What is the maximum time between BrakeWarn changing to 1 and the brake system warning telltale being lit?
findings.requirement_text: When BrakeWarn = 1, the cluster shall show the red brake system warning telltale steady on.

findings.explanation: Table 1 is not defined in this requirement set, so the telltales to be checked during the bulb check cannot be identified.
findings.question_for_author: Which document contains Table 1, and which telltales does it list?
findings.requirement_text: At each transition to the ACTIVE state, all telltales in Table 1 shall be lit for 2 s as a bulb check.

findings.explanation: It is not stated what priority means for telltales, for example display position, suppression of amber telltales, or arbitration of shared space, so no pass/fail test can be defined.
findings.question_for_author: What observable behaviour must occur when a red and an amber telltale are requested at the same time?
findings.requirement_text: Red telltales shall have priority over amber telltales.

findings.explanation: It is not stated whether the telltale must be lit steady or follow its normal pattern (for example flashing, as in G16), so the expected output on signal loss is unclear.
findings.question_for_author: In what mode (steady or flashing) must a telltale be lit when its input signal is missing?
findings.requirement_text: A telltale whose input signal has not been received for more than 500 ms shall be lit.

findings.evidence: within three times its cycle time
findings.explanation: This defines signal loss as three times the cycle time, while G21 and G22 use a fixed 500 ms, so the two timeout criteria disagree for any signal whose cycle time is not about 167 ms.
findings.question_for_author: Which timeout criterion defines a missing telltale input signal: three times the cycle time or a fixed 500 ms?
findings.requirement_text: If a CAN signal is not received within three times its cycle time, the cluster shall treat the signal as invalid.

findings.explanation: The chime priority list is not defined in this set, so the expected chime cannot be determined.
findings.question_for_author: Where is the chime priority list defined, and what does it contain?
findings.requirement_text: If two chimes are requested at the same time, the cluster shall play the chime with the higher priority as defined in the chime priority list.

findings.explanation: 'May' makes the behaviour optional, so no pass/fail result is possible.
findings.question_for_author: Is the display theme menu required, and if so, which themes must it offer?
findings.requirement_text: The cluster may offer a menu to change the display theme.

findings.explanation: No tolerance is given on the transmission period, so a test cannot decide whether a measured cycle time passes.
findings.question_for_author: What is the allowed tolerance on the ClusterStatus transmission period?
findings.requirement_text: The cluster shall transmit the ClusterStatus message every 100 ms.

findings.explanation: The referenced document is not identified by title or version, so the expected recovery behaviour cannot be determined.
findings.question_for_author: Which document, including identifier and version, defines the bus-off recovery behaviour?
findings.requirement_text: After a bus-off event, the cluster shall attempt recovery as specified in the network management document.

findings.explanation: The DTC code to be stored is not identified, so a test cannot check that the correct DTC was stored.
findings.question_for_author: Which DTC code shall be stored for a backlight driver fault?
findings.requirement_text: The cluster shall store a DTC when the display backlight driver reports a fault.

findings.explanation: The scope and checks of the display self-test are not defined, so it cannot be verified that the self-test was performed.
findings.question_for_author: What does the display self-test check, and where is it specified?
findings.requirement_text: The cluster shall perform a display self-test at startup.

findings.explanation: It is not stated how or to whom the result is reported (bus message, DTC, on-screen), so the expected output cannot be checked.
findings.question_for_author: Through which channel and to which recipient shall the self-test result be reported?
findings.requirement_text: The cluster shall report the result of the display self-test.

findings.explanation: What counts as a failed update is not defined, so the triggering conditions for the rollback cannot be tested.
findings.question_for_author: Which conditions constitute a failed update?
findings.requirement_text: If an update fails, the cluster shall return to the previously installed software version.

findings.explanation: No maximum time between detection and display of the warning is given, so the timing cannot be verified.
findings.question_for_author: What is the maximum time between detecting the mismatch and displaying the text warning?
findings.requirement_text: If a brake system warning telltale mismatch is detected, the cluster shall display a text warning.

findings.explanation: The content of the text warning is not defined, so a test cannot check that the correct warning is shown.
findings.question_for_author: What text shall the warning display, and where is it specified?
findings.requirement_text: If a brake system warning telltale mismatch is detected, the cluster shall display a text warning.

findings.evidence: When the fuel level is below 10 percent, the low-fuel telltale shall be lit.
findings.explanation: G14 lights the low-fuel telltale when the fuel level is below 10 percent, while G17 lights it on a different trigger, "When FuelLow = 1", so the same telltale has two different activation conditions.
findings.question_for_author: Which condition should switch on the low-fuel telltale: the cluster's own fuel level threshold, the FuelLow signal, or a defined combination of both?
findings.requirement_text: When the fuel level is below 10 percent, the low-fuel telltale shall be lit.
